headline: Medium risk: shared browser/file workflows can enable prompt injection and cascading errors; data leakage is limited by pdf.js no-egress defaults.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: next-ai-draw-io ingests PDFs, text, images, and diagram XML and uses MCP/browser-based AI-assisted visualization, so hostile file content can plausibly steer prompts. pdf.js renders PDFs in a browser worker, so if its output is copied into the other agent’s workflow, the pair has a realistic injection path. No shared channel is documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF next-ai-draw-io accepts untrusted PDF/text/diagram content as instructions
IF pdf.js output is copied into next-ai-draw-io without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction-following on imported files
Require a human review step before reusing pdf.js output
Tag imported content as untrusted in the workflow
Use separate workspaces for source files and generated prompts
requires-engineering: add provenance tracking between the two agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: next-ai-draw-io has broad network egress and handles API keys, while pdf.js reports no network egress and only PDF files. The pair can share PDFs, but the documented surfaces do not show a default path for pdf.js to exfiltrate data. Leakage risk exists mainly if the operator routes sensitive PDFs through next-ai-draw-io’s external APIs.
conditions: IF sensitive PDFs are processed by next-ai-draw-io using external model APIs
IF the same PDF workspace is shared and copied into networked workflows
mitigations: Keep sensitive PDFs in pdf.js only
Disable external API providers in next-ai-draw-io for sensitive jobs
Use separate folders for confidential and public documents
Rotate or avoid API keys in the processing environment
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss controls on outbound prompts

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances and both can operate on PDFs, creating overlapping write/processing pressure on the same documents if co-scheduled. next-ai-draw-io also uses MCP and browser-based workflows, which can mutate shared artifacts, while pdf.js is a browser worker. The profiles do not show locking, so conflicts are plausible in default multi-instance use.
conditions: IF both agents edit or regenerate the same PDF-derived artifact
IF multiple instances run against one shared workspace without locks
mitigations: Assign each agent its own output directory
Serialize edits to shared PDFs
Use file-level locks during generation
Keep pdf.js read-only for review tasks
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: next-ai-draw-io produces AI-assisted visualizations from documents, and pdf.js can supply rendered PDF content that may be treated as authoritative by the operator or downstream workflow. Because no verification step is documented between them, errors in one agent’s interpretation can cascade into diagrams or decisions made by the other. The interaction is inferred, so uncertainty raises severity to medium.
conditions: IF pdf.js output is reused as source-of-truth for next-ai-draw-io
IF generated diagrams are accepted without manual verification
mitigations: Require manual verification of extracted facts
Compare outputs against the original PDF before reuse
Mark generated diagrams as draft by default
Separate extraction from transformation steps
requires-engineering: add validation checks between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source document-processing tools, but next-ai-draw-io requests API keys and broad network egress while pdf.js is local-only. That creates a modest compliance mismatch around retention and third-party processing, not a residency or regulated-data breach by itself. The other agent is cited because the mismatch arises from the pair’s differing handling of the same documents.
conditions: IF regulated documents are sent through next-ai-draw-io’s external APIs
IF retention rules differ between local pdf.js review and networked processing
mitigations: Keep regulated documents in local-only pdf.js workflows
Disable cloud model providers for sensitive files
Document retention settings for each processing path
Separate public and regulated document queues
requires-engineering: align logging and retention policies
